Topic E — The Ignition–Extinction Diagram by Pseudo-Arclength Continuation

Topic B’s reactor with multiple steady states · folds · bordering algorithm · stability eigenvalues · tier: advanced (build B first)

Motivation

For strong enough heat release, topic B’s reactor has three steady states over a window of inlet temperatures: a cold (extinguished) one, a hot (ignited) one, and an unstable one between them. The branch of solutions turns back at two folds — the ignition and extinction temperatures. Natural continuation in T_\text{in} (Weeks 9 and 15) cannot pass a fold however small the step, because the branch is vertical there. Pseudo-arclength continuation (PAC) parameterises the branch by arclength and traces the whole S-curve.

Course weeks: topic B, 8–9 (Newton), 15 (continuation, §A3). New: the augmented system, tangent predictor, bordering algorithm, generalized eigenvalues for stability.

Model

Topic B’s equations, geometry and boundary conditions; the continuation parameter \lambda=T_\text{in}=T_\text{amb}. A reference computation found two folds for k_0\approx10^4, E\approx16, h_w=2 and more axial heat dispersion (k=0.2); finding parameters with a clear S-curve (start from a single-valued curve and increase k_0 or E) is part of the task.

PAC. With \mathbf F(\mathbf U;\lambda)=0 the discrete residual and (\dot{\mathbf U}_k,\dot\lambda_k) the unit tangent at the last point: predict \mathbf U^{(0)}=\mathbf U_k+\Delta s\,\dot{\mathbf U}_k, \lambda^{(0)}=\lambda_k+\Delta s\,\dot\lambda_k, then Newton on \mathbf F(\mathbf U;\lambda)=0,\qquad \dot{\mathbf U}_k^\top(\mathbf U-\mathbf U^{(0)})+\dot\lambda_k(\lambda-\lambda^{(0)})=0 . Bordering: each Newton step solves J\mathbf v=-\mathbf F and J\mathbf w=-\mathbf F_\lambda with the same factorised Jacobian, then \Delta\lambda=-(\phi+\dot{\mathbf U}_k^\top\mathbf v)/(\dot\lambda_k+\dot{\mathbf U}_k^\top\mathbf w), \Delta\mathbf U=\mathbf v+\Delta\lambda\,\mathbf w. \mathbf F_\lambda by a finite difference or exactly (UFL derivative of the forms with respect to a Constant; \lambda also enters through Dirichlet data).

Design output: the S-curve T_{\max}(T_\text{in}) (and X(T_\text{in})) through both folds; ignition and extinction temperatures.

Note

Analysis questions (required). (i) Why is J singular at a fold, and why is the bordered matrix not? (ii) Linear stability: perturbations e^{\sigma t}\mathbf v of the transient model give J\mathbf v=-\sigma M\mathbf v — which branch has a positive \sigma? (iii) Why can natural continuation “jump” to the other branch without any solver failure?

Required tasks

  1. Natural continuation reproduces your topic-B results where the curve is single-valued (consistency check of the PAC code with \dot\lambda>0 forced).
  2. Tangent computation and sign of \dot\lambda along the branch; PAC through both folds.
  3. Stability: the number of eigenvalues with \mathrm{Re}\,\sigma>0 of J\mathbf v=-\sigma M\mathbf v at points on each branch (0 / 1 / 0 expected) — slepc4py (in the %%fenicsx environment) or SciPy on a small mesh.
  4. Fold locations under refinement of \Delta s and of the mesh.

Verification specific to this topic

  • Branch connectivity: no gaps; every point a converged FE solution (print residual norms).
  • Fold detection two ways: sign change of \dot\lambda and an eigenvalue of J crossing zero at the same T_\text{in}.
  • 0D check: the CSTR (Semenov/van Heerden) heat balance has an S-curve with closed-form fold conditions — reproduce its qualitative shape with your PAC code applied to the 0D model before the PDE.
  • MMS for the steady topic-B system (as in topic B).

Stretch goals

  1. Adaptive \Delta s from the corrector’s iteration count.
  2. Direct fold localisation (extended system for J\dot{\mathbf U}=0).
  3. Two-parameter diagram: fold curves in the (k_0,T_\text{in}) plane.
  4. Deflation as an alternative way to find the middle branch.
  5. Check that the folds are not Hopf points (complex eigenvalues).

Milestones

M1 0D CSTR S-curve with your PAC code · M2 PDE natural continuation = topic B · M3 PAC through the first fold · M4 full S-curve and stability · M5 stretch goal.

Pitfalls

  • A corrector that needs many iterations while the bordering denominator stays away from zero is stiffness, not a fold — raise the iteration limit.
  • Near full conversion the upper branch becomes flat in T_\text{in}; trace it with natural continuation from a hot start instead of forcing PAC.
  • Scale the unknowns (and \lambda) to O(1) in the arclength norm, or \Delta s means nothing.

References

  • H. B. Keller, Numerical solution of bifurcation and nonlinear eigenvalue problems, in Applications of Bifurcation Theory, Academic Press 1977.
  • Yu. A. Kuznetsov, Elements of Applied Bifurcation Theory, Springer — folds and continuation.
  • C. van Heerden, Autothermic processes, Ind. Eng. Chem. 45 (1953) 1242–1247.
